subject: Geography
chapter: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature
central_question: How is solar energy received, redistributed and returned by the earth-atmosphere system, and how does this create temperature patterns?
in_scope_units: Variability and spatial distribution of insolation
Passage of solar radiation through the atmosphere
Conduction, convection, advection and terrestrial radiation
Heat budget and net radiation balance
Inversion of temperature and air drainage
banned_topics: Detailed pressure belts and circulation from Chapter 9
Detailed humidity and precipitation from Chapter 10
Detailed ocean-current systems from later oceanography chapters

known_pitfalls.claim: The atmosphere is mainly heated directly by incoming short-wave solar radiation.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter explains that the atmosphere is mainly heated indirectly from below by long-wave terrestrial radiation.

known_pitfalls.claim: The equator always receives the greatest surface insolation.
known_pitfalls.correction: Subtropical deserts can receive more because cloudiness is lower.
The normal lapse pattern can reverse during an inversion of temperature.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1(iv): match insolation, albedo, isotherm and annual range
NCERT Exercise 2(i): link unequal heat distribution with weather and climate
NCERT Exercise 3(i): explain latitude and axial tilt effects
NCERT Exercise 3(ii): explain earth-atmosphere heat balance
NCERT Exercise 3(iii): compare January temperature distribution in the hemispheres
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work using observatory temperature data.
